content.text:
Done. Three PNGs rendered at exact sizes from a single responsive `card.html`.

**Files:** `square.png` (1080×1080), `landscape.png` (1920×1080), `story.png` (1080×1920), plus the `card.html` source.

**How it works**
- One HTML document with a square master layout; landscape and story are aspect-ratio media queries (`min-aspect-ratio: 5/4` and `max-aspect-ratio: 4/5`) that retune a set of CSS variables (padding, avatar, type scale) and re-flow the layout.
- Inter is loaded via `@font-face` from the local `Inter.ttf` with `font-display: block`, so screenshots never capture a fallback-font flash.
- Layout per size: square stacks title over portrait+name; landscape splits into a text column (title capped at 1120px) and a centered portrait column; story goes full vertical with a full-width button.
- Portrait circularity is structural, not incidental: fixed square box + `aspect-ratio: 1/1` + `object-fit: cover` + `border-radius: 50%`, inside a violet gradient ring.

**Verification** — I wrote a temporary Playwright checker that loaded each viewport and asserted, against live DOM geometry: every element inside the padding safe area, no page scroll overflow, no pairwise overlap between the header/title/portrait/name/meta/button boxes, the avatar image exactly square with a 50% radius, and no clipped text. It initially flagged clipped text at all three sizes — that turned out to be glyph ink (descenders) spilling a few px past tight line-boxes with `overflow: visible`, i.e. a false positive rather than real cutoff. I fixed both sides: the checker now only flags overflow that is actually hidden, and I raised line-heights (1.18 on title and name, 1.2 on the event name) so the ink sits properly inside its lines. Final run was clean on all three, confirmed by eye on each render.

One judgment call worth flagging: I let the title wrap naturally rather than auto-fitting it to a fixed line count, so the three sizes break it at 3/3/4 lines respectively. If you'd rather it break identically across sizes, that needs a fixed line-break markup instead.
